usage_policy.principle: Rules-first Tarot: source-backed rules are converted to structured data; AI may phrase and synthesize but must not invent new rules.
usage_policy.copyright: Paraphrase and summarize copyrighted modern sources. Do not copy long passages or card interpretations from modern books/sites.
usage_policy.public_domain: Waite's Pictorial Key is used as the primary public-domain source for Rider-Waite-Smith meanings, still rewritten in Tarot voice.
usage_policy.source_traceability: Every major rule file should include source_basis or source_ids so future changes remain auditable.

sources.title: The Pictorial Key to the Tarot
sources.author: Arthur Edward Waite
sources.notes: Primary anchor for Rider-Waite-Smith. Language is old-fashioned; product copy should be rewritten.

sources.title: Book T - The Tarot
sources.author: Golden Dawn / Mathers-Felkin material
sources.notes: Use selectively for rules engine. Do not force full Golden Dawn astrology/qabalah into MVP unless explicitly needed.

sources.title: The Complete Book of Tarot Reversals
sources.author: Mary K. Greer
sources.notes: Use as framework, not copied text.

sources.title: Learning the Tarot
sources.author: Joan Bunning
sources.notes: Useful for readable, beginner-friendly reading structure.

sources.title: Learning Tarot Spreads
sources.author: Joan Bunning
sources.notes: Use to structure spread positions; do not copy full spread text.

sources.title: Seventy-Eight Degrees of Wisdom
sources.author: Rachel Pollack
sources.notes: Useful for depth and paid-reading tone, not a rigid rules engine.

sources.title: Holistic Tarot
sources.author: Benebell Wen
sources.notes: Very useful for product-oriented structure; do not copy copyrighted content.

sources.title: The Tarot: History, Symbolism, and Divination
sources.author: Robert M. Place
sources.notes: Use to avoid invented historical claims.

sources.title: Institutional references
sources.author: Britannica / V&A / Met / library collections
